newsitem.title: GERMANY: German coffee physicals slow, price pressure seen.
newsitem.headline: German coffee physicals slow, price pressure seen.

text.p: Cash coffee buyers in Germany are sitting on comfortable cover built in the first quarter and expect to see futures falls in the near term, traders said.
A sell-off in New York arabicas was possible after a larger than expected build-up of monthly stocks there on Friday, they added.
"There is a lot of coffee around in Europe and consumers are not interested in buying," one Bremen trader said.
"New York Dec arabicas may well be headed towards 150 cents/lb due to a lack of industry purchases."
The contract closed at 161.85 cents/lb, down 4.20, last Friday.
Coffee consumption here has weakened in the hot summer weather seen in recent weeks.
Importers said roasters were enquiring for new crop Central American but their price ideas were far below those of origin sellers.
Otherwise, sales were restricted to Centrals and Colombian ex-stock and distant shipping months.
Nominal arabica prices were $12-20 off on the week per 50 kg fob.
September shipment Brazils were at $165 second hand, Colombia excelso at $196, Guatemala HB at $220 and Sumatran robustas down $6 at $74, basis second hand cif.
